claims.claim: Lord Henry watches Basil in studio; portrait of Dorian Gray
claims.evidence: Chapter I; 'It is your best work, Basil, the best thing you have ever done'
'I can't exhibit it. I have put too much of myself into it.'

claims.claim: Dorian wishes portrait would age instead of him
claims.evidence: 'I who was to be always young, and the picture that was to grow old! ... I would give my soul for that!'

claims.claim: falls for Sibyl, rejects her, she kills herself
claims.evidence: 'Sibyl Vane was my sister. She killed herself.'; 'Sibyl Vane is dead.'

claims.claim: portrait shows cruelty; he hides it
claims.evidence: 'The portrait had altered.'; 'The portrait must be hidden away at all costs.'

claims.claim: murders Basil, who has seen the portrait
claims.evidence: 'the knife that had stabbed Basil Hallward'; Hallward: 'Let me see it.'
Campbell studied chemistry in a laboratory; Dorian: 'I have a letter written already... I must send it.'

claims.claim: James Vane hunting him accidentally shot dead
claims.evidence: Sir Geoffrey fires: 'I have hit a beater!'; 'The man who had been shot in the thicket was James Vane.'

claims.claim: Dorian stabs portrait; servants find it restored and a withered old man with knife in his heart
claims.evidence: 'a dead man ... with a knife in his heart. He was withered, wrinkled, and loathsome'
